queries.hook: When the darkness feels endless and the heart is too tired to go on, and no one seems to see the pain.
queries.diagnose: Fear grows from imagining the future and from forgetting that what is real in us cannot be lost; worry multiplies what has not happened.
queries.steady: This darkness is a passing night, not the whole of you; the self within you is whole, held and never alone.
queries.act: Hold on through the dark night and reach out to someone who cares; the self within you is not broken and is never alone.
queries.story: A story of a seeker whose mind will not settle, facing fear of what might happen.

understanding.life_context: Between things. Feels searching; closest to "I can't handle not knowing what comes next" and "I'm burned out and running on empty".

hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
hook.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
hook.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
hook.translation: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
hook.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

alternates.speaker: Rama
alternates.setting: Young Rama, back from his travels, tells the sages in his father's court why nothing interests him.
alternates.line: My heart feels heavy as stone, but I don't cry, because of what people would think.
alternates.translation: Though my heart is packed tight with the stones of life's sorrows, I don't let my tears fall, only out of fear of what my own people would think.
alternates.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
alternates.misuse: Holding tears in is not strength. Rama's healing began when he finally said it aloud.

matched.label: I'm burned out and running on empty

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

alternates.speaker: Rama
alternates.setting: Rama, ending his questions, asks for one practical skill.
alternates.sanskrit: व्यवहारवतो युक्त्या दुःखं नायाति मे यया । अथवा व्यवहारस्य ब्रूत तां युक्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥
alternates.line: Teach me how to keep working in the world without the work filling me with sorrow.
alternates.translation: Tell me the skill by which sorrow doesn't come to me while I go about my work, or else tell me the best way of dealing with life itself.
alternates.why: The real question isn't whether to quit life, but how to live it without being swallowed.

matched.label: I'm burned out and running on empty

prasang.title: Rama asks how to live in the world without being crushed by it
prasang.summary: After his lament Rama turns to questions. How did King Janaka and others stay free while running kingdoms? How can a person work in the world untouched, like water on a lotus leaf? He asks for one practical skill that lets him work without sorrow.
prasang.story_hook: Having said what was wrong, Rama finally asked the question that matters: how do the wise do it?
prasang.lesson: The real question isn't whether to quit life, but how to live it without being swallowed.

safety.message: If you're thinking about ending your life or harming yourself, please reach out now. You deserve support from a person.
